_about: Everything on retcalc.app that goes stale with time. One entry per thing to update. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD. last_updated: when the figures were last changed or checked against the source and found current. next_due: when to look again. Edit this file when an update is done, then run python3 upkeep/check.py --write. See upkeep/UPKEEP.md.

items.name: Federal income tax brackets and deductions
items.what: Federal brackets, standard deduction, long-term capital gains breakpoints, the age-65 extra standard deduction, and the 2025-2028 senior deduction.
where: web/lib/engine/data/<year>.js (2026.js today): fed, fedStd, ltcg, seniorAddl, seniorBonus. A new year is a new file; see UPKEEP.md
items.source: IRS revenue procedure for the coming tax year (Rev. Proc. 2025-32 gave 2026), usually out in late October
items.cadence: Yearly. Prepare in November or December; switch on January 1
items.notes: Statutory figures that are not indexed (NIIT, Social Security provisional-income thresholds) only change with a new law. The senior deduction ends after tax year 2028.

items.name: Retirement and HSA contribution limits, and the IRA deduction and Roth IRA phase-outs
items.what: 401(k)/403(b)/457 deferral limit and catch-ups (50+ and 60 to 63), the IRA limit and catch-up, HSA self-only and family limits and the 55+ catch-up, and the MAGI ranges over which a traditional IRA deduction phases out with a plan at work, and the MAGI ranges over which direct Roth IRA contributions phase out. Income Tax's pre-tax deductions pop-up warns against them and the engine applies the phase-out; the Budget tool's Paycheck tab points to a backdoor Roth past the Roth range (it never caps the line).
where: web/lib/engine/data/<year>.js: limits (k401, ira, hsa, iraPhase, rothPhase)

web/content/lessons/contribution-limits.html (the reference tables) and the other Saving and accounts lessons (where-each-dollar-goes, employer-match, traditional-or-roth, iras, hsa): 2026 limits, phase-outs and HDHP figures, some of them (SIMPLE, the total limit, pay cap, Roth catch-up wage line, HDHP figures) not in the data file
items.source: IRS notice on retirement plan limits (Notice 2025-67 gave 2026), usually out in late October or November; IRS revenue procedure on HSA limits (Rev. Proc. 2025-19 gave 2026), usually out in May
items.cadence: Yearly, with the new tax year
items.notes: The HSA catch-up ($1,000 from 55) is fixed by statute, not indexed. Added with the pre-tax deductions breakdown on Income Tax.

items.name: Social Security wage base, benefit bend points and earnings-test limits
items.what: The Social Security tax wage cap (also the cap on earnings the benefit estimate counts), the two bend points in the benefit formula, and the retirement earnings test's two exempt amounts (under full retirement age, and the year it's reached), which the claiming tool applies.
where: web/lib/engine/data/<year>.js: fica (fica.ssCap is the wage base, also the benefit estimate's earnings cap), ss.bend1, ss.bend2, ss.earn.under, ss.earn.fraYear

web/lib/engine/data/tables.js: SS_AWI, the national average wage index by year (add the newest year each October; ssa.gov/oact/cola/AWI.html). The calculator indexes past pay with the index two years before the data year
items.source: SSA's annual COLA and wage-base fact sheet, released in October
items.cadence: Yearly. Switch with the federal tax figures on January 1
items.notes: The wage base is one figure, fica.ssCap; the Social Security estimator reads it too. The earnings-test amounts are on the same SSA fact sheet; the Social Security Calculator and its About section quote the under-FRA one. 2027 figures gathered 2026-10-20 from SSA (oact/cola cbb.html, piaformula.html, rtea.html; released 2026-10-14): wage base $192,300; bend points $1,340 and $8,077; earnings test $25,560 under FRA and $67,920 in the year FRA is reached. 2025 average wage index (72,800.33) already added to SS_AWI. Owner: add them as data/2027.js on 2027-01-01 with the federal tax figures, not before (adding the year makes the calculator treat 2027 as the current year).

items.name: State income tax brackets and deductions (50 states and DC)
items.what: Every state's brackets, standard deduction, personal exemption and credits. Illinois has extra detail (exemption cliff, 65+ amount). Also which pre-tax deductions each state keeps in its base (states.preTaxed: Pennsylvania, New Jersey, California and Massachusetts as of 2026).
where: web/lib/engine/data/<year>.js: states.tax, states.preTaxed (and states.year, the year the state figures are for)
items.source: Tax Foundation, State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets (as of January 1), usually published in February; state revenue departments for detail
items.cadence: Yearly, after the Tax Foundation survey comes out
items.notes: States sometimes change rates mid-year; the law-watch item covers that. states.preTaxed changes only with a state law: check the 401(k), IRA, HSA and Section 125 treatment of PA, NJ, CA and MA, and watch for new non-conformers (New Jersey has had bills to allow 403(b), 457 and HSA deductions).

items.name: State rules for retirement income
items.what: Which states tax Social Security, pension and IRA exclusions, extra deductions or credits at 65, and states with no early-withdrawal penalty add-on.
where: web/lib/engine/data/<year>.js: states.retire, states.ssTaxed, states.noExpansion (Medicaid non-expansion; the plan engine and the Bridge)
items.source: State revenue departments; Tax Foundation and AARP state guides as a cross-check
items.cadence: Yearly, early in the year
items.notes: Several entries quote dollar amounts in their notes (Maryland's pension exclusion, Minnesota's AGI limits); those change yearly too.

items.name: Local income tax states and notes
items.what: Which states have local income taxes (and so show Income Tax's optional local field), each one's usual base (wages or state taxable income), its one-line note (Maryland's county range, New York City's range) and its lookup links.
where: web/tools/tax/local.ts: LOCAL_TAX
items.source: Tax Foundation's state and local income tax data; each state's revenue department (Maryland Comptroller county rates, New York tax department for NYC); check each lookup link still opens
items.cadence: Yearly, with the state tax update
items.notes: Rates are the person's own (nothing is computed from a built-in rate), so only the list of states, the notes' ranges and the links go stale. Left out on purpose: California and New Jersey (employer-paid local payroll taxes), Arkansas (allowed, none levied), Kansas (small local taxes on investment income).

items.name: Medicare Part B premium and IRMAA tiers
items.what: The standard Part B premium and the income tiers that raise Part B and Part D for higher earners.
where: web/lib/engine/data/<year>.js: medicare.irmaa (the Healthcare tool reads it through HC_IRMAA)
items.source: CMS Medicare Parts A and B premiums and deductibles fact sheet, usually out in October or November
items.cadence: Yearly. Switch on January 1

items.name: Medicare Part D and Medigap cost estimates
items.what: The average standalone Part D premium and the rough monthly range for a Medigap Plan G policy at 65.
where: web/lib/engine/data/<year>.js: medicare.partD, medicare.medigap (the plan engine and the Healthcare tool both read them)
items.source: CMS Part D premium announcement (summer); KFF or insurer surveys for Medigap
items.cadence: Yearly, in the fall
items.notes: One figure each now: the plan engine and the Healthcare tool share medicare.partD.

items.name: ACA marketplace premiums and subsidies
items.what: Average benchmark Silver premium by state, the poverty line the subsidies are measured against, the subsidy percentages, and whether the enhanced credits are back.
where: web/lib/engine/data/<year>.js: aca.fplBase, aca.fplPerAddl, aca.premium40, aca.cliff, aca.contrib (the applicable-percentage table)
web/tools/about/About.tsx: the '2026 rules' ACA text (the Healthcare tool names the year from the data)
web/components/dashboard/About.tsx: the Dashboard's copy of the same text
items.source: KFF Marketplace Average Benchmark Premiums (late October or November); HHS poverty guidelines (January, used for the next coverage year); IRS applicable-percentage revenue procedure (summer)
items.cadence: Yearly, for the coming coverage year
items.notes: Coverage year N is priced against the poverty guidelines published in January of N-1, so the 2026 guidelines (already out) are the ones for 2027 coverage.

items.name: RMD and life-expectancy tables
items.what: The IRS Uniform Lifetime Table (RMDs), the Single Life table (72(t) payments), and the RMD starting age, which works out birth year from the newest tax year in web/lib/engine/data/.
where: web/lib/engine/data/tables.js: ULT, BR_SLT (not by year)
web/lib/engine/math.js: rmdStartAge (reads the newest year from data/)
items.source: IRS Publication 590-B
items.cadence: Yearly check. The tables rarely change (last in 2022); rmdStartAge rolls with the newest tax year
items.notes: rmdStartAge computes birth year as the newest tax year minus age, so it rolls when a new year's file is added.

items.name: The tax year named in the site's text
items.what: Every place the site says '2026' about its rules: page titles and descriptions, tool badges and headings, the footer, preview cards, articles and FAQs.
where: web/lib/page-meta.json
web/lib/cards.ts
web/components/shell/Footer.tsx
web/components/dashboard/FinePrint.tsx (the Dashboard's copy of the disclaimer)
web/components/dashboard/About.tsx (the Dashboard's copy of the About tool sections: 2026 limits and rules, and the market record's last month)
web/content/articles/*.html
web/tools/**: 'grep -rn 2026 web --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx'. Most tools name the year from the data (yearData().year, NEWEST_YEAR); what's left is static text
items.source: Follows the tax items above
items.cadence: Yearly, on January 1, together with the federal switch
items.notes: Don't change a year that is about history (1926 to 2025) here; the market-history item covers those.

items.name: Stock, bond and inflation history
items.what: Monthly S&P 500 total returns, 10-year Treasury returns, CPI-U inflation and the historical CAPE series, January 1926 onward. Every historical test on the site runs on these.
where: web/lib/engine/data/history.js: HIST_M_STOCK, HIST_M_BOND, HIST_M_INFL, HIST_M_CAPE (and the '1,200 months' comment)
web/components/shell/Footer.tsx and the articles: '1926 to 2025'
web/tools/about/About.tsx and web/components/dashboard/About.tsx: Historical's 'January 1926 to December 2025' and its run counts
items.source: Robert Shiller's dataset (Yale), via multpl, for prices, dividends, yields and CAPE; US BLS for CPI-U (December's CPI comes out mid-January)
items.cadence: Yearly: add the past year's 12 months once December's data is in
items.notes: Moves many figures: the articles' worked examples, the homepage and Tools page figures, the numbers baseline, the Guide baseline, the e2e Guide figures, and possibly the preview cards. See UPKEEP.md.

items.name: Cash (T-bill) and small-cap value history
items.what: Monthly one-month Treasury bill and small-company value returns, July 1926 onward.
where: web/lib/engine/data/history.js: HIST_M_CASH, HIST_M_SV
items.source: Kenneth R. French Data Library (Dartmouth): the Fama-French factors file for T-bills, the 2x3 size/book-to-market portfolios for small value
items.cadence: Yearly, with the market history, once French posts December
items.notes: Must end on the same month as the market history, or the series fall out of step.

items.name: Today's CAPE reading
items.what: The latest Shiller CAPE, shown against the historical record and used by the CAPE withdrawal strategy's 'today' figures.
where: web/lib/engine/data/history.js: CAPE_NOW, CAPE_NOW_ASOF
web/content/lessons/cape-valuations.html: today's CAPE in the prose, a table and In short (search the lessons for the old reading)
items.source: multpl.com Shiller PE (monthly)
items.cadence: Monthly
items.notes: check.py reads last_updated and data_for from CAPE_NOW_ASOF, and sets next_due to that date plus max_age_days. Keep the string a plain 'day Month year' date.

items.name: Default mortgage rate
items.what: The 30-year rate the Mortgage and Rent vs. Buy tools start with. The pages call it a starting point, not a live quote.
where: web/lib/engine/data/tables.js: MORT_RATE_30 (and its comment)
items.source: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey (weekly); use a rounded recent average
items.cadence: Quarterly, or sooner if rates move more than half a point
items.notes: Changing it moves the Mortgage and Rent vs. Buy figures in the numbers baseline and their articles' worked examples.

items.name: Home price, rent and housing-cost defaults
items.what: The starting home price, rent, rent growth, home appreciation, property tax rate and insurance in the Mortgage and Rent vs. Buy tools.
where: web/tools/mortgage/model.ts: MORTGAGE_DEFAULTS
web/tools/rentbuy/model.ts: RENTBUY_DEFAULTS
items.source: NAR or Census median home price; Census or Zillow median rent; Tax Foundation property tax rates
items.cadence: Yearly
items.notes: Round figures on purpose; only change when they're clearly off.

items.name: College cost presets
items.what: The yearly cost of a public in-state and a private school (tuition, room and board) the College Savings tool offers.
where: web/tools/college/model.ts: the presets and default kid
web/content/articles/college.html: the worked example
web/components/dashboard/Profile.tsx and college.ts: the Dashboard's school choices (public, private, elite) repeat the presets
items.source: College Board, Trends in College Pricing (published in late October)
items.cadence: Yearly, after College Board publishes
items.data_for: College Board Trends in College Pricing 2025 (2025-26): $25,850 public in-state and $60,920 private non-profit for tuition, fees, housing and food, rounded to $26,000 and $61,000
items.notes: The article quotes $26,000 and monthly saving figures the tests check. The elite preset ($82,000) has no College Board figure behind it.

items.name: What children cost (the Guide and Paycheck to Retirement)
items.what: Monthly cost of a child by age: everyday costs before school ($1,300), 6 to 12 ($1,400) and 13 to 18 ($1,500); childcare on top by area (big city $1,500, suburb or small city $1,000, rural $700); 20% less for a later child. Rounded to $100.
where: web/tools/guide/schedule.ts: CHILD_COST and the source line CHILD_SOURCE
web/tools/about/About.tsx: the Guide's 'Children and other changes' figures and the 'What children cost' source line
items.source: USDA, Expenditures on Children by Families, 2015 (middle-income married couples, Table 1), brought to today's prices with the CPI-U; Department of Labor Women's Bureau, National Database of Childcare Prices (center care, by county size), brought forward with the CPI for day care and preschool
items.cadence: Yearly: carry both forward with the CPI; switch to a newer USDA study or childcare-price release when one comes out
items.notes: USDA middle-income totals for ages 6-11 and 12-17 (teens about 5% more), and ages 0-5 less child care and education. Childcare from 2018 county medians in 2022 dollars (infants: $8,310 in counties under 100,000 people, $17,171 at 1 million or more), averaged over ages 0 to 5 and brought forward. Changing them moves the Guide's numbers for plans with children: re-record the numbers baseline.

items.name: 72(t) interest rate floor
items.what: The Bridge's 72(t) interest rate starts at 5%, which is always allowed: the IRS permits the greater of 5% or 120% of the federal mid-term rate. This is a check that 5% is still the statutory floor, not a default to chase.
where: web/tools/bridge/model.ts: seppRate (default 5)
web/lib/glossary.ts: brsepprate
web/content/articles/72t.html and bridge.html: the worked examples use 5%
web/content/lessons/rule-72t.html: the dated 120%-of-mid-term figures
items.source: IRS Notice 2022-6 (the 5% floor); IRS Applicable Federal Rates (monthly revenue rulings) for the 120% test
items.cadence: Yearly: confirm Notice 2022-6 still sets the 5% floor and that no later notice or law changed it. Do not move the default when the mid-term rate rises
items.data_for: 5% (Notice 2022-6: the greater of 5% or 120% of the federal mid-term rate)
items.notes: If the floor changes, change the default, the glossary entry and the articles' worked examples together (tests/math.test.js checks them). The lesson's dated figures (120% of the mid-term rate was 5.40% in September and 5.54% in October 2026) are reviewed with the lessons.

items.name: Debt Payoff example rates
items.what: The example debts' interest rates, mainly the credit card APR.
where: web/tools/debt/model.ts: ROWS
web/content/articles/debt.html (if it quotes them)
items.source: Federal Reserve G.19 consumer credit report (credit card rates)
items.cadence: Yearly
items.notes: The tests check the article's worked example against these.

items.name: Long-run assumption defaults
items.what: Default return before inflation (8.5%), inflation (3%), college cost growth (4%), heirs' tax rate and similar starting assumptions.
where: web/lib/engine/calculators.js: DEFAULTS, BASIC_DEFAULTS, RISK_LEVELS
web/tools/*/model.ts: each tool's defaults
web/lib/engine/plan.js: PL_HEIR
items.source: Long-run history on the site itself; Vanguard and Morningstar capital-market outlooks as a sanity check
items.cadence: Yearly review; change rarely
items.notes: These are judgment calls, not data. Raise any change with the owner first.

items.name: New laws that change the rules mid-year
items.what: Federal or state legislation that changes brackets, deductions, ACA subsidies (the enhanced credits that expired after 2025), RMD ages or Social Security taxation between the yearly updates.
where: Wherever the law lands; usually the year's file in web/lib/engine/data/, math.js and the articles
items.source: IRS newsroom, Tax Foundation tracker, KFF for ACA, state revenue departments
items.cadence: Quarterly check

items.name: Article reviews ('Last reviewed' month)
items.what: Each tool page's article shows the month it was last reviewed. A review means checking its figures, sources and links still hold; only then move its date.
where: web/content/articles/*.html: data-reviewed on each <article>
items.source: The article's own sources and the site's current figures
items.cadence: Each article every 90 days (set max_age_days to change it)
items.notes: check.py reads every article's data-reviewed date: last_updated is the oldest, next_due is that plus max_age_days. Run node web/scripts/lastmod.mjs after editing an article.

items.name: Learn lesson reviews ('Last reviewed' month) and their outside links
items.what: Each Learn lesson shows the month it was last reviewed. A review means checking every figure, rule and research claim it quotes against the site's current data and its sources, and that each Go deeper link still opens and says what it's cited for; only then move its date.
where: web/content/lessons/*.html: data-reviewed on each <article>; the Go deeper links in each <footer>
items.source: The site's data files (web/lib/engine/data/), the tool articles, and each lesson's own sources
items.cadence: Each lesson every 90 days (set max_age_days to change it); also whenever a figure it quotes changes (new tax year, Medicare premiums, Trustees Report, CAPE)
items.notes: check.py reads every lesson's data-reviewed date. Lessons quote this year's limits, brackets, Medicare and ACA figures, Social Security figures and today's CAPE: when one of those items is updated, search content/lessons/ for the old figure too.
